title_en: Important Notes on Taking Cross-Listed Courses
summary: This notice sets out how credit is recognised and how retakes must be registered when students take cross-listed courses. A cross-listed course taken under a major other than the student's own is recognised as a general elective.
applies_to: Students who take, or wish to retake, cross-listed courses.
steps: When registering for a cross-listed course, note that a course from another major (not your own) that is cross-listed will be credited as a general elective [일반선택].

If you wish to retake a cross-listed course, register for the section offered under the same course number as the course you originally completed. For example, if courses A and B are cross-listed and you completed course A, you must register for course A to retake it.
translation:
Important Notes on Taking Cross-Listed Courses

Please review the following notes on taking cross-listed courses.

※ Please note that if you take a cross-listed course offered under another major that is not your own, the credits will be recognised as a general elective [일반선택].

○ (Credit recognition) When a student takes a cross-listed course, the grade is recorded on the transcript as completion of the course under the specific major for which the student registered.

○ (Retaking a course) If a student wishes to retake a cross-listed course, the student must register for the section offered under the course number of the course previously completed.

※ Example: if courses A and B are cross-listed, and a student has completed course A and wishes to retake it, the retake is possible only if the student registers for course A, the course previously completed.
